D: A group of young ranch hands become outlaws after their mentor is murdered in New Mexico.
P: Serve the mains when Tunstall's boys sit down at his ranch table.
S: the English rancher who teaches the boys manners
Cucumber and butter, and ham and mustard sandwiches, crusts off, cut into triangles, a proper English touch on a New Mexico ranch.
Roasted green chillies chopped into a hot cheese dip of cheddar melted into evaporated milk with garlic, with tortilla chips.

Thin-sliced beef topside marinated in Worcestershire, soy, cracked pepper and chilli, dried low in the oven until chewy and dark. Freeze 800g beef topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick against the grain. Mix 80ml Worcestershire sauce, 40ml soy sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp cracked black pepper and 1 tsp chilli flakes. Marinate the beef overnight in the fridge. Pat dry, press on more pepper and lay on wire racks over trays. Dry at 70C with the door ajar for 4 hours until leathery. Cool and store airtight.
M: Beef chuck browned and braised slowly with onion, carrot, potato and toasted dried red chillies until thick and rich, with warm flour tortillas. Toast 4 dried red chillies in a dry pan, soak in 300ml hot water for 20 minutes and blitz smooth. Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 onions and 3 garlic cloves, add 1 tsp cumin, the chilli puree and 500ml beef stock, and return the beef. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours. Add 2 carrots and 500g potatoes in chunks and cook 1 hour more. Serve with warm flour tortillas.
Pork shoulder in chunks browned, braised 2.5 hours with roasted green chillies, tomatillos, onion, garlic and cumin until it falls apart, served over rice.
W: Butter and sugar creamed with aniseed, flour worked in, rolled and cut into stars, dipped in cinnamon sugar, baked at 175C for 10 minutes until pale gold.
K: Rye whisky stirred down over ice with demerara syrup and aromatic bitters, poured over one big ice cube with a wide strip of orange peel. Stir 50g demerara sugar into 50ml hot water to make a syrup and cool. For each drink, fill a mixing glass with ice and add 60ml rye whisky, 10ml of the syrup and 2 dashes aromatic bitters. Stir for 30 seconds until very cold. Strain over a large ice cube in a short glass. Squeeze a wide strip of orange peel over the top and drop it in.

s.note: the English rancher who teaches the boys manners
s.how: Butter 8 slices white bread. Fill half with thin cucumber and half with 150g ham and English mustard. Cut off the crusts and cut into triangles for a proper English touch on a New Mexico ranch.

Roast 3 green chillies until blackened, peel and chop. Warm 375ml evaporated milk with a crushed garlic clove, stir in 250g grated cheddar until smooth, then add the chillies. Serve hot with a 300g bag of corn chips.

m.how: Brown 1.2kg diced pork shoulder. Char 4 green chillies and 400g tomatillos, then blitz with an onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp cumin. Braise the pork in the sauce for 2.5 hours until it falls apart. Serve over 300g rice.

w.how: Beat 200g butter with 100g sugar and 1 tsp crushed aniseed, then work in 300g flour. Roll out and cut into stars. Dip the tops in sugar mixed with cinnamon and bake at 175C for 10 minutes until pale gold.

d.how: Stir 50g demerara sugar into 50ml hot water to make a syrup and cool. For each drink, fill a mixing glass with ice and add 60ml rye whisky, 10ml of the syrup and 2 dashes aromatic bitters. Stir for 30 seconds until very cold. Strain over a large ice cube in a short glass. Squeeze a wide strip of orange peel over the top and drop it in.
